text: Everyone needs to get freakishly realistic about where you stand in the social hierarchy, what league you are playing in, because I am so sick of seeing everyone try to shoot for the 10% of either gender, either gender. But you know what? Guess what? The 10% are dating each other, so there is logically no point for you trying to shoot that high above yourself. She says everyone is shooting for the top 10%, but that's just not true. Let's be real, most men aren't chasing the top 10% of women. Most guys are simply trying to get the reply, a match, or a date with any woman they find attractive and compatible. The data actually proves it. Studies from Tinder and OkCupid show that the majority of women receive a large amount of attention online, not just the so-called top 10%. Even average-looking women get dozens or hundreds of likes, while the average guy barely gets noticed. That means men aren't all chasing the same few girls, they are just trying their shot with whoever seems real and approachable, while women are the ones filtering most of it out. In fact, the real imbalance is the other way around. Research shows that about 20% of men get around 80% of the likes and messages from women. So when someone says everyone is aiming too high, they are actually describing female behavior, not male. The average man isn't delusional, he is just invisible. He is not sitting there expecting a model, he is trying to get someone to respond. Meanwhile, women complain that men aim too high, when in reality, they are the ones swiping past 90% of men without a second thought. That's the brutal truth of modern dating. It's not that men are all chasing supermodels, it's that most women are chasing the same small group of men, and then wondering why all men are players.
